sections.title: Basic Concept
sections.content: The average (arithmetic mean) of a set of numbers is the sum of the numbers divided by the total count. Formula: Average = (Sum of observations) / (Number of observations). Example: Average of 10, 20, 30 = (10+20+30)/3 = 60/3 = 20.

sections.title: Average in Daily Life
sections.content: Averages are used to find middle values. Example: If 5 students scored 40, 50, 60, 70, 80 marks, the average score = (40+50+60+70+80)/5 = 60. It helps in quick assessment of performance.

sections.title: Relationship with Sum and Number of Observations
sections.content: If average of n numbers is A, then sum of numbers = n × A. Conversely, if sum and count are known, average = sum / n. Example: Average of 8 numbers = 25 → Sum = 8 × 25 = 200.

sections.title: Using Deviations from Average
sections.content: The sum of deviations of all numbers from their average is always 0. Example: Numbers: 10, 20, 30; Average = 20; Deviations: -10, 0, 10; Sum = 0.

sections.title: Combining Two Groups
sections.content: If group 1 has n1 numbers with average A1 and group 2 has n2 numbers with average A2, the combined average = (n1×A1 + n2×A2) / (n1 + n2). Example: 5 students average 40, 10 students average 50 → Combined average = (5×40 + 10×50)/15 = 46.67.

sections.title: Finding Missing Observation
sections.content: If average of n numbers is known and n-1 numbers are known, the missing number = (Average × n) - Sum of known numbers. Example: Average of 5 numbers = 20, known numbers = 15, 25, 18, 22 → Missing number = (20×5) - (15+25+18+22) = 100 - 80 = 20.

sections.title: Quick Check for Average
sections.content: If all numbers are increased or decreased by same value, average increases or decreases by same value. Example: Numbers 10, 20, 30 → Average = 20. Add 5 to each → New average = 25.

tricks.title: Shortcut for Equal Deviations
tricks.explanation: If numbers are equally spaced, average = middle number.
tricks.example: Numbers: 12, 15, 18 → Middle number 15 is the average.

tricks.title: Weighted Average Trick
tricks.explanation: Multiply each group average by its size, sum, and divide by total size.
tricks.example: Class A: 10 students avg 50, Class B: 20 students avg 60 → Combined avg = (10×50 + 20×60)/30 = 56.67.

tricks.title: Reverse Average Trick
tricks.explanation: Given sum and average, find total count = sum / average.

tricks.title: Missing Number Quick Formula
tricks.explanation: Missing = (Average × total count) - sum of known numbers.

tricks.title: Average after Increase/Decrease
tricks.explanation: Add/subtract same value to all numbers → Add/subtract to average.
tricks.example: Avg of 5 numbers = 40 → Add 5 to each → New avg = 45.

tricks.title: Simplified Sum Calculation
tricks.explanation: Sum = Average × Number of terms, helps quick calculation without adding all numbers.

tricks.title: Using Midpoint for Odd Number Series
tricks.explanation: For odd consecutive numbers, average = middle number.

tricks.title: Balancing Positive and Negative Deviations
tricks.explanation: Sum of deviations from average = 0, useful for verification.

tricks.title: Weighted Adjustments for Groups
tricks.explanation: When combining groups with different averages, always consider group sizes.
tricks.example: Group1: 3 numbers avg 10, Group2: 2 numbers avg 20 → Combined avg = (3×10 + 2×20)/5 = 14.

tricks.title: Quick Estimation
tricks.explanation: For approximate average, round numbers and then divide sum by count.
